items.title: OpenAI says agents are accelerating research
items.oneliner: OpenAI says researchers now use 3.1 agent-workdays per human day. Labs are already reorganizing around machine coworkers.

items.title: Microsoft is testing autonomous Office workflows
items.oneliner: Project Opal turns Copilot into a multi-step office agent. Enterprise automation is moving from chat to execution.

items.title: vLLM brings speculative decoding to AMD
items.oneliner: vLLM added speculative decoding on AMD GPUs. Cheaper inference stacks just got more credible outside Nvidia.

items.title: An outdated Forgejo server was compromised
items.oneliner: Attackers lived on a Forgejo server for a month, created 94 accounts, and ran a miner. Patch lag still kills.

items.title: LG TVs were caught logging audio
items.oneliner: LG TVs reportedly logged audio with screens off and scanned local devices. Consumer hardware is still hostile by default.

items.title: Nitter will keep fighting X legally
items.oneliner: After X sent cease and desist letters, Nitter says it will continue. Privacy-preserving frontends are now legal battlegrounds.

items.title: AI audit found Bitcoin code flaws
items.oneliner: A volunteer team says AI found 85 critical Bitcoin flaws across 390 repos in 27.5 hours. Security review is speeding up.

items.title: Tottenham cut VMware costs by 85 percent
items.oneliner: Tottenham says its VMware exit cut licensing fees by over 85 percent. Broadcom pricing is finally forcing real migrations.

items.title: TPMs can sign live TLS handshakes
items.oneliner: Signing TLS handshakes inside a TPM makes key theft materially harder. Hardware-backed identity is getting practical for services.

items.title: Rust developers want better debugging tools
items.oneliner: Rust's 2026 debugging survey drew 2,300 responses, and 46 percent actively use debuggers. Tooling gaps are still adoption friction.
